astronomy noun

classical

Cic. Div. 2.87; Cic. Off. 1.19 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 274

astrologia, astrologiae f.

noun, first declension

astronomy, the knowledge of the stars

The classical word for astronomy; Lewis & Short notes that it came to mean astrology alone only in late Latin, when astronomia took the older sense.

Other words

  • astronomia, astronomiae f. — astronomy

    noun, first declension · also used · post-classical · Lewis & Short s.v. astrologia; Traupman 274

  • astrologus, astrologī m. — an astronomer

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Varr. RR 2.1.7; Cic. Div. 2.87 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 274

See also astrology.

SourcesLewis & Short: astrologia · Lewis & Short: astrologus
